Please solve this issue: The Tokyo office wants Fizzy in Japanese, upstream says internationalization
is never coming, so it lands on us.

Make the app speak more than one language. Japanese has to ship complete: a
person who chose Japanese gets every screen and every email in Japanese,
dates included. Nothing readable may stay hardcoded English — the text a
screen reader announces is readable too.

Opening any page with `?locale=ja` switches that person to Japanese, and the
choice sticks: for the rest of their session, and again the next time they
sign in from a clean browser. A locale we don't offer (`?locale=xx`) never
breaks a page — it just doesn't switch anything.

People who never chose anything must not notice any of this
happened: their pages keep rendering exactly the English they render today.
One exception: the static error pages are served without knowing who is
looking, so render those in both languages.

The rich-text editor ships its own strings inside its JavaScript package.
Leave those alone.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

**Initial Assessment: Configuration and Structure**

Alright, I'm zeroing in on this list: `config/application.rb`, `config/locales/en.yml`, `config/ci.rb`, `config/routes.rb`, `db/schema.rb`, and `public/*.html`. Immediately, my mind starts categorizing. `application.rb` will be the heart of the application's overall configuration. I'm expecting to find settings related to middleware, load paths, and perhaps some initializers or environment-specific configurations. `config/locales/en.yml` is the localization file, likely holding all the English translations and text keys. This is crucial for internationalization, and I'll be looking for well-structured keys and potential areas for improvement in translation management if it's a large project.

`config/ci.rb` is intriguing. I bet this file contains configuration for the continuous integration process; probably build steps, testing frameworks, and potentially deployment scripts for the CI server. The `config/routes.rb` is where the application's URL structure is defined. I'll be looking at the routing constraints, resource definitions, and any custom routes to understand the flow and accessibility of various application components. Then we have `db/schema.rb`, the database schema. This file is generated by ActiveRecord and I expect to see the structure of the database tables, including data types, indexes, and any constraints. It will be helpful to understand database relationships.

Finally, the `public/*.html` files are, of course, the static HTML files served directly by the web server. These are the basic templates and starting points. I'll need to know whether any of them are just placeholders, or if they contribute to the application's overall structure. I want to know where they are linking to, if any of the dynamic content is contained within them and where the application will pick it up, or if they are entirely separate. My immediate goal is to understand how these elements interrelate and how the application is structured at a high level. Let's get to work!

steps.reasoning_content:
**Comprehensive I18n Implementation for Fizzy**

Okay, so this is about more than just a quick translation job; it's a complete internationalization (i18n) overhaul for Fizzy, specifically targeting Japanese. I need to make sure this is done meticulously. First, the application must support multiple languages, but Japanese needs to be fully supported from day one. This means every single piece of text visible to a Japanese user *must* be in Japanese: every screen, every email, including date formats. Nothing can be hardcoded English, including what a screen reader would announce. Accessibility is critical.

The implementation needs to be smart. A user choosing Japanese via `?locale=ja` needs the setting to "stick" for the rest of their session *and* the next time they sign in from a clean browser. Crucially, I have to figure out how this choice is persisted – likely in the database on either the `Identity` or `User` model, or perhaps both – and how that interacts with the login flow, including magic links. What happens with unauthenticated users visiting `?locale=ja`? What happens with people switching locales? What about unsupported locales like `?locale=xx`? It shouldn't break anything. And if someone signs up with the `?locale=ja` preference, their first e-mail will *also* need to be in Japanese!

A huge caveat: Users who *don't* choose a language should see no change. The existing English experience needs to be exactly the same, as per the existing tests. This means no automatic language detection based on the `Accept-Language` header. This needs to be bullet-proof, especially in tests that expect specific English strings. The only exception is the static error pages, which, since they are served without knowing the user's locale, must render in both languages.

Finally, the rich-text editor (Lexxy) is a black box, so whatever strings it ships internally are not to be touched. But I still need to check that our app's own customizations of the editor, like `aria-label` or placeholders, are translated.

Now, let's dive into the codebase and analyze all the models, views, controllers, mailers, and background jobs to pinpoint every single piece of translatable text and ensure a comprehensive and correct translation, focusing heavily on date and time handling.

# Fix for SQLite FTS5 virtual table schema dumping
# Rails has a bug where it doesn't handle FTS5 content= and content_rowid= options

module SQLiteFTS5SchemaDumperFix
  # Override the virtual_tables method to handle FTS5 syntax properly
  def virtual_tables(stream)
    # Query sqlite_master for all virtual tables
    virtual_table_sqls = @connection.select_rows(
      "SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND sql LIKE 'CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE%'"
    )

    virtual_table_sqls.each do |table_name, sql|
      # Just output the raw SQL since create_virtual_table doesn't handle our syntax
      stream.puts "  execute #{sql.inspect}"
      stream.puts
    end
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record_sqlite3adapter) do
  ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::SQLite3::SchemaDumper.prepend(SQLiteFTS5SchemaDumperFix)
end

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_action :require_account # Checking and setting account must happen first
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :authenticated?
    helper_method :email_address_pending_authentication

    etag { Current.identity.id if authenticated? }

    include Authentication::ViaMagicLink, LoginHelper
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_authenticated_user, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :resume_session, **options
      allow_unauthorized_access **options
    end

    def disallow_account_scope(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_account, **options
      before_action :redirect_tenanted_request, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticated?
      Current.identity.present?
    end

    def require_account
      unless Current.account.present?
        redirect_to main_app.session_menu_path(script_name: nil)
      end
    end

    def require_authentication
      resume_session || authenticate_by_bearer_token || request_authentication
    end

    def resume_session
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def find_session_by_cookie
      Session.find_signed(cookies.signed[:session_token])
    end

    def authenticate_by_bearer_token
      if request.authorization.to_s.include?("Bearer")
        if bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
          authenticate_or_request_with_http_token do |token|
            if identity = Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token(token, method: request.method)
              Current.identity = identity
            end
          end
        else
          request_http_token_authentication
        end
      end
    end

    def bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
      request.format.json?
    end

    def request_authentication
      if Current.account.present?
        session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      end

      redirect_to_login_url
    end

    def after_authentication_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || landing_url
    end

    def redirect_authenticated_user
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if authenticated?
    end

    def redirect_tenanted_request
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if Current.account.present?

# Repair task — reindexes every searchable Card and Comment in the database.
# Intended to be invoked manually after a search-index loss event. Not a recurring job.
#
# Idempotent: Searchable#reindex upserts by (searchable_type, searchable_id).
# Continuable: if the worker is interrupted, the job resumes from the last-processed id.
#
# `rich_text_limit` is a safety valve against unbounded bodies: records whose rich text
# exceeds the limit (in bytes) are filtered out at the SQL level, so they never materialize
# in Ruby. Without it, a single pathological body can stall the batch query or OOM the
# worker during preload, which has happened in practice.
#
# Usage:
#   SearchReindexJob.perform_later
#   SearchReindexJob.perform_later(batch_size: 500, log_every: 100, rich_text_limit: 50_000)
class SearchReindexJob < ApplicationJob
  include ActiveJob::Continuable

  queue_as :backend

  def perform(batch_size: 100, log_every: 1000, rich_text_limit: 100_000)
    step :cards do |step|
      processed = 0
      Card.published
          .left_joins(:rich_text_description)
          .where("action_text_rich_texts.body IS NULL OR OCTET_LENGTH(action_text_rich_texts.body) <= ?", rich_text_limit)
          .includes(:rich_text_description)
          .find_each(start: step.cursor, batch_size: batch_size) do |card|
        safely_reindex(card)
        processed += 1
        log_progress(:cards, processed, card.id) if (processed % log_every).zero?
        step.advance! from: card.id
      end
    end

    step :comments do |step|
      processed = 0
      Comment.joins(:card).merge(Card.published)
             .left_joins(:rich_text_body)
             .where("action_text_rich_texts.body IS NULL OR OCTET_LENGTH(action_text_rich_texts.body) <= ?", rich_text_limit)
             .includes(:rich_text_body, :card)
             .find_each(start: step.cursor, batch_size: batch_size) do |comment|
        safely_reindex(comment)
        processed += 1
        log_progress(:comments, processed, comment.id) if (processed % log_every).zero?
        step.advance! from: comment.id
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def safely_reindex(record)
      record.reindex
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.error.report(e, context: { record_type: record.class.name, record_id: record.id })
    end

    def log_progress(step_name, count, cursor)
      Rails.logger.info { "SearchReindexJob: step=#{step_name} processed=#{count} cursor=#{cursor}" }
    end
end
# Serializes the current account into job data so that jobs run
# within the correct account context via Current.with_account.
#
# Account resolution is deferred to an around_perform callback so
# that missing accounts raise DeserializationError inside the
# execution path where discard_on can handle it.
module AccountTenanted
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  prepended do
    attr_reader :account
    around_perform :with_account_context
  end

  def initialize(...)
    super
    @account = Current.account
  end

  def serialize
    super.merge({ "account" => @account&.to_gid })
  end

  def deserialize(job_data)
    super
    @account_gid = job_data["account"]
  end

  private
    def with_account_context(&block)
      resolve_account!

      if account.present?
        Current.with_account(account, &block)
      else
        yield
      end
    end

    def resolve_account!
      if @account_gid
        @account = GlobalID::Locator.locate(@account_gid)
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      raise ActiveJob::DeserializationError
    end
end

This is a *critical* starting point, as the `@identity` might not even have a `User` associated with it yet, or even exist in the current account's context. *   **Mailer 2:** `ImportMailer` (both `completed` and `failed`) directly addresses the `identity`. Importantly, `ImportMailer#failed` deals with a case where the `account` might not even exist, as it's triggered from a background job (`Account::Import`). This presents the *biggest* localization challenge. We MUST ensure that the recipient's language preference dictates the content, *regardless* of the context in which the notification was generated (e.g., Alice's language). Bob, who chose Japanese, *must* get Japanese emails and push notifications. This is a crucial insight! We need to decouple the generation language from the recipient's display language.

# Adds a helper method to check if replica database connections are configured
# and automatically configures read/write splitting when replicas are available.
#
# Usage:
#   class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
#     configure_replica_connections
#   end
module ActiveRecordReplicaSupport
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    # Automatically configures connects_to for read/write splitting if a replica
    # database is configured for the current environment. This is a no-op if no
    # replica configuration exists.
    #
    # Example:
    #   class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
    #     configure_replica_connections
    #   end
    def configure_replica_connections
      if replica_configured?
        connects_to database: { writing: :primary, reading: :replica }
      end
    end

    # Returns true if a replica database configuration exists for the current
    # environment. This allows different database adapters to opt in or out of
    # read/write splitting based on their database.yml configuration.
    #
    # Example:
    #   ApplicationRecord.replica_configured? # => true for MySQL, false for SQLite
    def replica_configured?
      configurations.find_db_config("replica").present?
    end

    # Execute block using read replica if available, otherwise use primary.
    #
    # Example:
    #   ApplicationRecord.with_reading_role { User.count }
    def with_reading_role(&block)
      if replica_configured?
        connected_to(role: :reading, &block)
      else
        yield
      end
    end
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
  include ActiveRecordReplicaSupport
end

# Apply MySQL-compatible column limits when defining tables.
#
# For string columns: defaults to 255 (MySQL's VARCHAR default)
#
# For text columns: converts MySQL's `size:` option to equivalent limits:
#   - (blank/default): 65,535 (TEXT)
#   - size: :tiny: 255 (TINYTEXT)
#   - size: :medium: 16,777,215 (MEDIUMTEXT)
#   - size: :long: 4,294,967,295 (LONGTEXT)
#

module TableDefinitionColumnLimits
  TEXT_SIZE_TO_LIMIT = {
    tiny: 255,
    medium: 16_777_215,
    long: 4_294_967_295
  }.freeze

  TEXT_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 65_535
  STRING_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 255

  def column(name, type, **options)
    if type == :string
      options[:limit] ||= STRING_DEFAULT_LIMIT
    end

    if type == :text || type == :binary
      if options.key?(:size)
        size = options.delete(:size)
        options[:limit] ||= TEXT_SIZE_TO_LIMIT.fetch(size) do
          raise ArgumentError, "Unknown text size: #{size.inspect}. Use :tiny, :medium, or :long"
        end
      elsif type == :text
        options[:limit] ||= TEXT_DEFAULT_LIMIT
      end
    end

    super
  end
end

# For SQLite: append inline CHECK constraints to enforce string/text length limits.
# since SQLite doesn't natively enforce VARCHAR/TEXT length limits.
module SQLiteColumnLimitCheckConstraints
  def add_column_options!(sql, options)
    super

    column = options[:column]
    if column && column.limit && %i[string text].include?(column.type)
      check_expr = if column.type == :string
        # VARCHAR limits are in characters
        %(length("#{column.name}") <= #{column.limit})
      else
        # TEXT limits are in bytes
        %(length(CAST("#{column.name}" AS BLOB)) <= #{column.limit})
      end
      sql << " CHECK(#{check_expr})"
    end

    sql
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
  ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::TableDefinition.prepend(TableDefinitionColumnLimits)
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record_sqlite3adapter) do
  ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::SQLite3::SchemaCreation.prepend(SQLiteColumnLimitCheckConstraints)
end

  class DatabaseResolver < ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector::Resolver
    def self.in_primary_datacenter?

  "output_head": "#!/usr/bin/env bash

fi

fi

# gum is a mise-managed tool, so it isn't installed yet on a fresh machine.
step() {
  local step_name="$1"
  shift

  # gum may resolve to a mise shim that aborts before this config is trusted or
  # mise meets the floor — and the shim dir is configurable, so probe by running
  # gum rather than matching paths. Any failure falls back to plain echo.
  if gum --version &> /dev/null; then
    gum style --foreground 135 --bold "▸ $step_name"
    gum style --foreground 240 "$*"
  else
    echo "▸ $step_name"
    echo "$*"
  fi

  "$@"

  local exit_code=$?
  echo
  return $exit_code
}

mise_min_version="2026.7.10" # keep in lockstep with min_version in .mise.toml

mise_too_old() {
  local current="$(mise --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $1; exit }')"
  [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$mise_min_version" "$current" | sort -V | head -1)" != "$mise_min_version" ]
}

ensure_correct_mise_install() {
  if ! command -v mise &> /dev/null; then
    # brew installs are a macOS decision — a Linuxbrew host must not gain a
    # brew-owned mise moments before the manager gate rejects or ignores it
    if [ "$(uname -s)" = Darwin ] && command -v brew &> /dev/null; then
      # refresh the formula index first: a stale one (fresh VM images, long-idle
      # machines) resolves an old mise and the version floor is unreachable
      brew update --quiet || true
      brew install mise
    elif command -v pacman &> /dev/null; then
      sudo pacman -S --noconfirm --needed mise
    else
      echo "Please install mise: https://mise.jdx.dev/"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi

  if mise_too_old; then
    # Upgrade the ACTIVE mise, classified by the resolved binary's owner — a brew
    # keg can coexist with the pacman/dpkg/mise.run install PATH actually
    # resolves, and upgrading an inactive copy would leave the floor unmet.
    mise_path="$(readlink -f "$(command -v mise)")"
    if command -v brew &> /dev/null && [[ "$mise_path" = "$(brew --prefix)"/* ]]; then
      # refresh the formula index first: with a stale one (fresh VM images,
      # long-idle machines) brew considers an old mise current and this upgrade
      # is a no-op — found live on the fresh-macOS signoff VM
      brew update --quiet || true
      brew upgrade mise || true
    elif command -v pacman &> /dev/null && pacman -Qo "$mise_path" &> /dev/null; then
      sudo pacman -Syu --noconfirm mise || true
    else
      mise self-update --yes --no-plugins || true
    fi
  fi

  if mise_too_old; then
    echo "mise $mise_min_version or newer is required. Please upgrade mise and rerun bin/setup."
    exit 1
  fi
}

  if [ "$CI" != "" ]; then

  fi

  if [ "$has_data" = "true" ] ; then
    return 1

}

My initial thought was that a simple `session[:locale]` would do the trick, but `session`s can be cleared or overridden, and only represent a single browser session. If the user signs in as `kevin` and sets the locale to `"ja"`, I need to make sure that setting is preserved even after `kevin` logs out and then signs back in, or if `david` logs in on the same browser.  The trick here is to ensure that the *most recent* locale preference wins, and to correctly handle the case where a user *prefers* a locale *before* signing in.

Here's the new plan:

1.  **When a locale is set via `?locale=ja`:** The plan is to set `session[:locale] = "ja"`. If the user is authenticated, update `authenticated_identity.locale = "ja"`. If unauthenticated, `session[:pending_locale] = "ja"`. This applies to any page on which a valid `?locale=...` is present.

I've looked at all the mailers in detail: `AccountMailer`, `ExportMailer`, `ImportMailer`, `MagicLinkMailer`, `Notification::BundleMailer`, and `UserMailer`. Right, `parameterize` strips those non-ASCII characters, which results in `""` – an empty string! Thankfully, it seems like explicitly passing `key:` (or falling back to the MD5 digest) could keep English IDs consistent (since `parameterize` works fine there), while giving Japanese titles unique, *stable* keys.  Ideally, we'd pass the English key so the users' UI settings in local storage are stable, even when switching languages. This would also keep tests for those elements working regardless of language. Second, the `to_sentence` method scattered across `FiltersHelper`, `CardsHelper`, `BridgeHelper`, and `NotificationsHelper` caught my eye.  Rails' `Array#to_sentence` uses `I18n` with the `support.array.words_connector`, `two_words_connector`, and `last_word_connector` translations. That's actually pretty elegant. This means that if we configure `ja.yml` properly for `support.array` (with Japanese connectors like "、" and "と"), we'll get *naturally* grammatically correct Japanese sentences.     # Finds a Color by its CSS value (e.g. "var(--color-card-4)").
    # Falls back to extracting the value from legacy export formats where
    # the Color struct was serialized instead of the raw CSS string.
    def for_value(value)
      COLORS.find { |it| it.value == value } ||
        extract_from_legacy_export(value)
    end

    private
      # Broken exports serialized Color structs instead of raw CSS values,
      # producing JSON like {"name":"Lime","value":"var(--color-card-4)"}.
      # Parse it and extract the value.
      def extract_from_legacy_export(value)
        parsed = value.is_a?(String) && JSON.parse(value)
        COLORS.find { |it| it.value == parsed["value"] } if parsed.is_a?(Hash)
      rescue JSON::ParserError
      end
  end

  def to_s
    value
  end

  COLORS = {
    "Blue" => "var(--color-card-default)",
    "Gray" => "var(--color-card-1)",
    "Tan" => "var(--color-card-2)",
    "Yellow" => "var(--color-card-3)",
    "Lime" => "var(--color-card-4)",
    "Aqua" => "var(--color-card-5)",
    "Violet" => "var(--color-card-6)",
    "Purple" => "var(--color-card-7)",
    "Pink" => "var(--color-card-8)"
  }.collect { |name, value| new(name, value) }.freeze
end

class Filter < ApplicationRecord
  include Fields, Params, Resources, Summarized

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }
  belongs_to :account, default: -> { creator.account }

  class << self
    def from_params(params)
      find_by_params(params) || build(params)
    end

    def remember(attrs)
      create!(attrs)
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      find_by_params(attrs).tap(&:touch)
    end
  end

  def cards
    @cards ||= begin
      result = creator.accessible_cards.preloaded.published
      result = result.indexed_by(indexed_by)
      result = result.sorted_by(sorted_by)
      result = result.where(id: card_ids) if card_ids.present?
      result = result.where.missing(:not_now) unless include_not_now_cards?
      result = result.open unless include_closed_cards?
      result = result.unassigned if assignment_status.unassigned?
      result = result.assigned_to(assignees.ids) if assignees.present?
      result = result.where(creator_id: creators.ids) if creators.present?
      result = filter_boards(result) if boards.present?
      result = result.tagged_with(tags.ids) if tags.present?
      result = result.where(cards: { created_at: creation_window }) if creation_window
      result = result.closed_at_window(closure_window) if closure_window
      result = result.closed_by(closers) if closers.present?
      result = terms.reduce(result) do |result, term|
        result.mentioning(term, user: creator)
      end
      result = result.where(column_id: column_ids) if column_ids.present?

      result.distinct
    end
  end

  def empty?
    self.class.normalize_params(as_params).blank?
  end

  def single_board
    boards.first if boards.one?
  end

  def single_workflow
    boards.first.workflow if boards.pluck(:workflow_id).uniq.one?
  end

  def cacheable?
    boards.exists?
  end

  def cache_key
    ActiveSupport::Cache.expand_cache_key params_digest, "filter"
  end

  def only_closed?
    indexed_by.closed? || closure_window || closers.present?
  end

  private
    def filter_boards(relation)
      relation = relation.where(cards: { account_id: creator.account_id }).where(board: boards.ids)
      if joins_has_many?
        relation
      else
        # Pin the (account_id, last_active_at, status) index so the ordered page is served by a reverse scan, not a filesort.
        relation.use_index(:index_cards_on_account_id_and_last_active_at_and_status)
      end
    end

    # Assignee, tag, and term filters add a has-many join that fans a card into
    # several rows; the ordered reverse scan loses to a different plan then, so
    # the pin only applies without them.
    def joins_has_many?
      assignees.present? || tags.present? || terms.present?
    end

    def include_closed_cards?
      only_closed? || card_ids.present?
    end

    def include_not_now_cards?
      indexed_by.not_now? || card_ids.present?
    end
end

class Signup::AccountNameGenerator
  SUFFIX = "Fizzy".freeze

  attr_reader :identity, :name

  def initialize(identity:, name:)
    @identity = identity
    @name = name
  end

  def generate
    next_index = current_index + 1

    if next_index == 1
      "#{prefix} #{SUFFIX}"
    else
      "#{prefix} #{next_index.ordinalize} #{SUFFIX}"
    end
  end

  private
    def current_index
      existing_indices.max || 0
    end

    def existing_indices
      Current.without_account do
        identity.accounts.filter_map do |account|
          if account.name.match?(first_account_name_regex)
            1
          elsif match = account.name.match(nth_account_name_regex)
            match[1].to_i
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def first_account_name_regex
      @first_account_name_regex ||= /\A#{prefix}\s+#{SUFFIX}\Z/i
    end

    def nth_account_name_regex
      @nth_account_name_regex ||= /\A#{prefix}\s+(1st|2nd|3rd|\d+th)\s+#{SUFFIX}/i
    end

    def prefix
      @prefix ||= "#{first_name}'s"
    end

    def first_name
      name.strip.split(" ", 2).first
    end
end

class Passkey::Authenticator < Data.define(:aaguids, :name, :icon)
  class << self
    def find_by_aaguid(aaguid)
      registry[aaguid]
    end

    def registry
      @registry ||= Hash.new.tap do |registry|
        all.each do |authenticator|
          authenticator.aaguids.each do |aaguid|
            registry[aaguid] = authenticator
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def all
      Rails.application.config_for(:passkey_aaguids).each_value.map do |attrs|
        new(aaguids: attrs[:aaguids], name: attrs[:name], icon: attrs[:icon])
      end
    end
  end
end

class TimeWindowParser
  attr_reader :now

  HUMAN_NAMES_BY_VALUE = {
    "today" => "Today",
    "yesterday" => "Yesterday",
    "thisweek" => "This week",
    "thismonth" => "This month",
    "thisyear" => "This year",
    "lastweek" => "Last week",
    "lastmonth" => "Last month",
    "lastyear" => "Last year"
  }

  VALUES = HUMAN_NAMES_BY_VALUE.keys

  class << self
    def parse(string)
      new.parse(string)
    end

    def human_name_for(value)
      HUMAN_NAMES_BY_VALUE[value]
    end
  end

  def initialize(now: Time.current)
    @now = now
  end

  def parse(string)
    case normalize(string)
    when "today"
      now.all_day
    when "yesterday"
      (now - 1.day).all_day
    when "thisweek"
      now.all_week
    when "thismonth"
      now.all_month
    when "thisyear"
      now.all_year
    when "lastweek"
      (now - 1.week).all_week
    when "lastmonth"
      (now - 1.month).all_month
    when "lastyear"
      (now - 1.year).all_year
    end
  end

  private
    def normalize(string)
      if string
        string.downcase.gsub(/[\s_\-]/, "")
      end
    end

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include ActionView::Helpers::TagHelper

  def export_json
    JSON.pretty_generate({
      number: number,
      title: title,
      board: board.name,
      status: export_status,
      creator: export_user(creator),
      description: export_html(description),
      created_at: created_at.iso8601,

      comments: comments.chronologically.map do |comment|

          body: export_html(comment.body),

          created_at: comment.created_at.iso8601
        }
      end
    })
  end

  def export_attachments
    collect_attachments.map do |attachment|
      { path: export_attachment_path(attachment.blob), blob: attachment.blob }
    end
  end

  private
    def export_html(rich_text)
      return "" if rich_text.blank?

      rich_text.body.render_attachments do |attachment|
        attachment_representation(attachment)
      end.to_html
    end

    def attachment_representation(attachment)
      case attachable = attachment.attachable
      when ActiveStorage::Blob
        path = export_attachment_path(attachable)
        if attachable.image?
          tag.img(src: path, alt: attachable.filename)
        else
          tag.a(attachable.filename, href: path)
        end
      when ActionText::Attachables::RemoteImage
        tag.img(src: attachable.url, alt: "Remote image")
      else
        attachment.to_html
      end
    end

    def export_user(user)
      {
        id: user.id,
        name: user.name,
        email: user.identity&.email_address
      }
    end

    def export_attachment_path(blob)
      "#{number}/#{blob.key}_#{blob.filename}"
    end

    def collect_attachments
      (attachments.to_a + comments.flat_map { |c| c.attachments.to_a }).uniq(&:blob_id)
    end

      case
      when closed?
        "Done"
      when postponed?
        "Not now"
      when column.present?
        column.name
      else
        "Maybe?"
      end
    end

Let's break this down:

1.  **Identity & User Locale Methods**:
    *   **Identity**: We're validating the `locale` field to ensure it's a supported locale and allowing it to be `nil`. We have `preferred_locale`, which returns the locale only if it's set and valid. The `in_locale` method uses `I18n.with_locale` to execute a block of code with the user's preferred locale or the default if none is set. `update_locale` is really smart - it normalizes the locale, checks availability, and updates the locale in a database transaction, only if there's a change.
    *   **User**: This is where we're defaulting to the identity's preferred locale, or the default if the identity is missing. There's an `in_locale` method, which aligns to the same usage of the identity model.
    *   **Current**: We've added a `:session_locale` attribute, which is so smart. Now `Identity#send_magic_link` can be passed the `Current.session_locale` so that the locale is preserved. This is a very elegant solution!

2.  **CurrentLocale Controller Concern**:
    *   This is the heart of the locale-switching magic. We include this concern early in the `ApplicationController`—before authentication! That makes sense, because the callbacks run in the order they're registered. So we wrap the entire request in `set_current_locale`. The system retrieves either the `requested_locale` from the URL params or uses `find_session_by_cookie&.identity` to determine the user's identity, *even before authentication*.

    *   `available_locale` checks `params[:locale]`. Crucially, if the locale is invalid (`nil`, empty, not a string, or not supported), it *never* raises an error, it *never* modifies the session, and it *never* modifies the `identity.locale`. The whole function is really well-designed.

    *   Now, we check if there's an authenticated `identity`. If there is, we set the `session[:locale] = requested_locale` if there is a locale requested and update the identity's locale. If there is *no* authenticated identity, it just sets `session[:pending_locale]` to the requested locale.

    *   The really smart part: `Current.session_locale` is set to the available version of the session locale.

    *   How we determine the active locale is what's really important:

        *   **Case 1**: If a `requested_locale` parameter is present (`?locale=ja` or `?locale=en`), then that's the chosen locale.
        *   **Case 2**: If no parameter is passed, we check if the user is signed in:
            *   If they *are* signed in, their latest `identity.preferred_locale` from *any* browser should win, or the `session[:locale]` if one exists.
                *   If `pending_locale` is set, and the identity is present, it will get synced using `identity.update_locale(pending_locale)`.
                *   Even if the `session_token` cookie is injected *without* signing in, `pending_locale` gets synced to `identity`.
            *   Then it uses the user's preferred locale, the session locale if present, and finally the default locale. The code accounts for all possible scenarios and the order of precedence is perfect.

    *   **Very important corner cases**: If a user logs out, they stay in their chosen language for the browser session. If a new user signs in, they are not impacted by the previous user's chosen locale.

    *   What about routing? If a user opens `/signup?locale=ja`, we need to preserve the `locale` parameter in the redirect, so the user can sign up in their desired language.

module Notification::Pushable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    class_attribute :push_targets, default: []

    after_save_commit :push_later, if: :source_id_previously_changed?
  end

  class_methods do
    def register_push_target(target)
      target = resolve_push_target(target)
      push_targets << target unless push_targets.include?(target)
    end

    private
      def resolve_push_target(target)
        if target.is_a?(Symbol)
          "Notification::PushTarget::#{target.to_s.classify}".constantize
        else
          target
        end
      end
  end

  def push_later
    Notification::PushJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def push
    return unless pushable?

    user.in_locale do
      self.class.push_targets.each { |target| push_to(target) }
    end
  end

  def payload
    "Notification::#{payload_type}Payload".constantize.new(self)
  end

  private
    def pushable?
      !creator.system? && user.active? && account.active?
    end

    def push_to(target)
      target.process(self)
    end

    def payload_type
      source_type.presence_in(%w[ Event Mention ]) || "Default"
    end
end

Then, all controller flash messages, alerts, and JSON responses must be internationalized. Next, I'll tackle all of the models and Lib: `Event::Description`, `Card::Eventable::SystemCommenter`, and the rest of the alphabet. After that come the helpers and mailers, and their views. A lot of work there!

Then, all 332 view files are up next. Layouts, Turbo Streams, the PWA manifest - the whole lot! And finally, the locale files themselves. This is where the organization becomes critical. I'm thinking of loading individual YAML files from `config/locales/en/` and `config/locales/ja/` directories, alongside the main `en.yml` and `ja.yml` files, using `config.i18n.load_path` – this will keep things modular, clean, and conflict-free, and it will be easy to review. Plus, our automated key-parity tests can check the dictionaries against each other!

I'll start by enabling that `load_path` configuration, right away.

Wait, hold on! Before I even touch a single view, model, or helper... I need to capture English golden snapshots of key pages! This is crucial. Remember the requirement: "People who never chose anything must not notice any of this happened: their pages keep rendering exactly the English they render today." This is where the golden snapshot comes in.

If I write a script right now to render key pages—login, home, boards, cards, notifications, user settings, search, webhooks, and all the emails— and captures the raw HTML output, I can compare the translated output against this baseline. Anything changes, even the smallest punctuation mark will be caught immediately. This transforms the "hope" of meeting the requirement into **mathematical certainty**!

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/color.rb
Color = Struct.new(:name, :value)

class Color
  class << self
    # Finds a Color by its CSS value (e.g. "var(--color-card-4)").
    # Falls back to extracting the value from legacy export formats where
    # the Color struct was serialized instead of the raw CSS string.
    def for_value(value)
      COLORS.find { |it| it.value == value } ||
        extract_from_legacy_export(value)
    end

    private
      # Broken exports serialized Color structs instead of raw CSS values,
      # producing JSON like {"name":"Lime","value":"var(--color-card-4)"}.
      # Parse it and extract the value.
      def extract_from_legacy_export(value)
        parsed = value.is_a?(String) && JSON.parse(value)
        COLORS.find { |it| it.value == parsed["value"] } if parsed.is_a?(Hash)
      rescue JSON::ParserError
      end
  end

  def to_s
    value

class Event::Description
  include ActionView::Helpers::TagHelper
  include ERB::Util

  attr_reader :event, :user

  def initialize(event, user)
    @event = event
    @user = user
  end

  def to_html
    to_sentence(creator_tag, card_title_tag).html_safe
  end

  def to_plain_text
    to_sentence(creator_name, quoted(card.title)).html_safe
  end

  private
    def to_sentence(creator, card_title)
      if event.action.comment_created?
        comment_sentence(creator, card_title)
      else
        action_sentence(creator, card_title)
      end
    end

    def creator_tag
      tag.span data: { creator_id: event.creator.id } do
        tag.span(I18n.t("events.description.you"), data: { only_visible_to_you: true }) +
        tag.span(event.creator.name, data: { only_visible_to_others: true })
      end
    end

    def card_title_tag
      tag.span card.title, class: "txt-underline"
    end

    def creator_name
      h event.creator.name
    end

    def quoted(text)
      I18n.t("events.description.quoted", text: h(text))
    end

    def card
      @card ||= event.action.comment_created? ? event.eventable.card : event.eventable
    end

    def comment_sentence(creator, card_title)
      I18n.t("events.description.commented", creator: creator, card: card_title)
    end

    def action_sentence(creator, card_title)
      case event.action
      when "card_assigned"
        assigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_unassigned"
        unassigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_published"
        I18n.t("events.description.published", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_closed"
        I18n.t("events.description.closed", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_reopened"
        I18n.t("events.description.reopened", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_postponed"
        I18n.t("events.description.postponed", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_auto_postponed"
        I18n.t("events.description.auto_postponed", card: card_title)
      when "card_resumed"
        I18n.t("events.description.resumed", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_title_changed"
        renamed_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_board_changed", "card_collection_changed"
        moved_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_triaged"
        triaged_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_sent_back_to_triage"
        I18n.t("events.description.sent_back_to_triage", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      end
    end

    def assigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      if event.assignees.include?(user)
        I18n.t("events.description.assigned_self", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      else
        I18n.t("events.description.assigned_others", creator: creator, assignees: assignee_names, card: card_title)
      end
    end

    def unassigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      I18n.t("events.description.unassigned", creator: creator, assignees: unassigned_names, card: card_title)
    end

    def renamed_sentence(creator, card_title)
      I18n.t("events.description.renamed", creator: creator, card: card_title, old_title: old_title)
    end

    def moved_sentence(creator, card_title)
      I18n.t("events.description.moved", creator: creator, card: card_title, location: new_location)
    end

    def triaged_sentence(creator, card_title)
      I18n.t("events.description.triaged", creator: creator, card: card_title, column: column)
    end

    def assignee_names
      h event.assignees.pluck(:name).to_sentence
    end

    def unassigned_names
      h(event.assignees.include?(user) ? I18n.t("events.description.yourself") : assignee_names)
    end

    def old_title
      h event.particulars.dig("particulars", "old_title")
    end

    def new_location
      h(event.particulars.dig("particulars", "new_board") || event.particulars.dig("particulars", "new_collection"))
    end

    def column
      h event.particulars.dig("particulars", "column")
    end
end

class Notification::EventPayload < Notification::DefaultPayload
  include ExcerptHelper

  def title
    case event.action
    when "comment_created"
      I18n.t("notifications.push.comment_title", title: card_title)
    else
      card_title
    end
  end

  def body
    creator = event.creator.name

    case event.action

      format_excerpt(event.eventable.body, length: 200)
    when "card_assigned"
      I18n.t("notifications.push.card_assigned", creator: creator)
    when "card_published"
      I18n.t("notifications.push.card_published", creator: creator)
    when "card_closed"
      card.closure ? I18n.t("notifications.push.card_moved_to_done", creator: creator) : I18n.t("notifications.push.card_closed", creator: creator)
    when "card_reopened"
      I18n.t("notifications.push.card_reopened", creator: creator)
    when "card_triaged"
      if column_name.present?
        I18n.t("notifications.push.card_triaged_to", column: column_name, creator: creator)
      else
        I18n.t("notifications.push.card_moved", creator: creator)
      end
    when "card_sent_back_to_triage"
      I18n.t("notifications.push.card_sent_back_to_triage", creator: creator)
    when "card_board_changed", "card_collection_changed"
      if new_location_name.present?
        I18n.t("notifications.push.card_board_changed_to", location: new_location_name, creator: creator)
      else
        I18n.t("notifications.push.card_moved", creator: creator)
      end
    when "card_title_changed"
      if new_title.present?
        I18n.t("notifications.push.card_renamed_to", title: new_title, creator: creator)
      else
        I18n.t("notifications.push.card_renamed", creator: creator)
      end
    when "card_postponed"
      I18n.t("notifications.push.card_postponed", creator: creator)
    when "card_auto_postponed"
      I18n.t("notifications.push.card_auto_postponed")
    else
      I18n.t("notifications.push.card_updated", creator: creator)
    end
  end

  def url
    case event.action
    when "comment_created"
      card_url_with_comment_anchor(event.eventable)
    else
      card_url(card)
    end
  end

  def category
    case event.action
    when "card_assigned" then "assignment"
    when "comment_created" then "comment"
    else "card"
    end
  end

  def high_priority?
    event.action.card_assigned?
  end

  private
    def event
      notification.source
    end

    def card_title
      card.title.presence || I18n.t("notifications.push.card_fallback_title", number: card.number)
    end

    def event_particulars
      event.particulars.dig("particulars") || {}
    end

    def column_name
      event_particulars["column"]
    end

    def new_location_name
      event_particulars["new_board"] || event_particulars["new_collection"]
    end

    def new_title
      event_particulars["new_title"]
    end

    def card_url_with_comment_anchor(comment)
      card_url(comment.card) + "##{ActionView::RecordIdentifier.dom_id(comment)}"
    end
end

steps.message: Let's internationalize `Signup::AccountNameGenerator` and `Account::Seeder` for newly signed-up Japanese accounts while keeping English identical.
steps.reasoning_content:
**A Perfect Run and a Localization Boost!**

Okay, so the CI is looking good – 642 model tests, zero failures, zero RuboCop offenses, and not a single Brakeman warning. *Excellent!* Time to shift gears a bit. We need to make sure our Japanese users get the right experience when they sign up. The current implementation uses `Signup::AccountNameGenerator` to generate account names and `Account::Seeder` to seed the initial playground board and onboarding cards.

Right now, if a new user selects `:ja` (Japanese) for their locale during signup, we need to adapt both processes. The generated account name should shift from the current format to something more appealing for Japanese users, like "#{first_name}のFizzy". Additionally, we have to make sure the seeded playground board title (`プレイグラウンド`) and the initial onboarding cards are localized to Japanese. This means we'll need to add `signup` and `seeder` keys to the `config/locales/{en,ja}/seeder.yml` files. After that, I'll update `app/models/signup/account_name_generator.rb` and `app/models/account/seeder.rb` to pull this new locale information, ensure the Japanese users get the Japanese account name, and see their boards and cards in Japanese from the get-go. This should improve the onboarding experience and make them feel more at home in the application. Let's get these updates rolled out!

cat <<'EOF' > app/helpers/accesses_helper.rb
module AccessesHelper
  def access_menu_tag(board, **options, &)
    tag.menu class: [ options[:class], { "toggler--toggled": board.all_access? } ], data: {
      controller: "filter toggle-class navigable-list",
      action: "keydown->navigable-list#navigate filter:changed->navigable-list#reset",
      navigable_list_focus_on_selection_value: true,
      navigable_list_actionable_items_value: true,
      toggle_class_toggle_class: "toggler--toggled" }, &
  end

  def access_toggles_for(users, selected:, disabled: false)
    render partial: "boards/access_toggle",
      collection: users, as: :user,
      locals: { selected: selected, disabled: disabled },
      cached: ->(user) { [ user, selected, disabled ] }
  end

  def access_involvement_advance_button(board, user, show_watchers: true, icon_only: false)
    access = board.access_for(user)

    turbo_frame_tag dom_id(board, :involvement_button) do
      concat board_watchers_list(board) if show_watchers
      concat involvement_button(board, access, show_watchers, icon_only)
    end
  end

  def board_watchers_list(board)
    watchers = board.watchers.with_avatars.load

    displayed_watchers = watchers.first(8)
    overflow_count = watchers.size - 8

    tag.div(class: "divider divider--fade") do
      tag.strong(watchers.any? ? t("helpers_ui.accesses.watching_for_new_cards") : t("helpers_ui.accesses.no_one_watching"), class: "txt-uppercase")
    end +
    tag.div(avatar_tags(displayed_watchers), class: "board-tools__watching") do
      tag.div(data: { controller: "dialog", action: "keydown.esc->dialog#close click@document->dialog#closeOnClickOutside" }) do
        tag.button("+#{overflow_count}", class: "overflow-count btn btn--circle borderless", data: { action: "dialog#open" }, aria: { label: t("helpers_ui.accesses.show_more_watchers", count: overflow_count) }) +
        tag.dialog(avatar_tags(watchers), class: "board-tools__watching-dialog dialog panel", data: { dialog_target: "dialog" }, aria: { hidden: "true" })
      end if overflow_count > 0
    end
  end

  def involvement_button(board, access, show_watchers, icon_only)
    label_text = access.access_only? ? t("helpers_ui.accesses.watch_this") : t("helpers_ui.accesses.stop_watching")
    button_to(
      board_involvement_path(board), method: :put,
      params: { show_watchers: show_watchers, involvement: next_involvement(access.involvement), icon_only: icon_only },
      aria: { labelledby: dom_id(board, :involvement_label) },
      title: (label_text if icon_only),
      class: class_names("btn", { "btn--reversed": access.watching? && icon_only }),
      data: !icon_only && { bridge__overflow_menu_target: "item", bridge_title: label_text }) do
        icon_tag("notification-bell-#{icon_only ? 'reverse-' : nil}#{access.involvement.dasherize}") +
        tag.span(label_text, class: class_names("txt-nowrap txt-uppercase", "for-screen-reader": icon_only), id: dom_id(board, :involvement_label))
    end
  end

  private
    def next_involvement(involvement)
      order = %w[ watching access_only ]
      order[(order.index(involvement.to_s) + 1) % order.size]
    end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/helpers/application_helper.rb
module ApplicationHelper
  def page_title_tag
    account_name = if Current.account && Current.session&.identity&.users&.many?
      Current.account&.name
    end
    tag.title [ @page_title, account_name, "Fizzy" ].compact.join(" | ")
  end

  def icon_tag(name, **options)
    tag.span class: class_names("icon icon--#{name}", options.delete(:class)), "aria-hidden": true, **options
  end

  def back_link_to(label, url, action, prefer_referrer: [], **options)
    data = { controller: "hotkey", action: action }
    if prefer_referrer.any?
      data[:turbo_navigation_target] = "referrerBackLink"
      data[:turbo_navigation_allowed_referrer_paths] = prefer_referrer.join(",")
    end
    link_to url, class: "btn btn--back btn--circle-mobile", data: data, **options do
      icon_tag("arrow-left") + tag.strong(t("helpers_ui.application.back_to", label: label), class: "overflow-ellipsis") + tag.kbd("ESC", class: "txt-x-small hide-on-touch").html_safe
    end
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/helpers/pagination_helper.rb
module PaginationHelper
  def pagination_frame_tag(namespace, page, data: {}, **attributes, &)
    turbo_frame_tag pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page.number), data: { timeline_target: "frame", **data }, role: "presentation", **attributes, &
  end

  def link_to_next_page(namespace, page, activate_when_observed: false, label: default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed), data: {}, **attributes)
    if page.before_last? && !params[:previous]
      attributes[:class] = class_names(attributes[:class], "btn txt-small center-block center": !activate_when_observed)
      pagination_link(namespace, page.number + 1, label: label, activate_when_observed: activate_when_observed, data: data, **attributes)
    end
  end

  def pagination_link(namespace, page_number, activate_when_observed: false, label: default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed), url_params: {}, data: {}, **attributes)
    link_to label, url_for(params.permit!.to_h.merge(page: page_number, **url_params)),
      "aria-label": t("helpers_ui.pagination.load_page", page: page_number),
      id: "#{namespace}-pagination-link-#{page_number}",
      class: class_names(attributes.delete(:class), "pagination-link", { "pagination-link--active-when-observed" => activate_when_observed }),
      data: {
        frame: pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number),
        pagination_target: "paginationLink",
        action: ("click->pagination#loadPage:prevent" unless activate_when_observed),
        **data
      },
      **attributes
  end

  def pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number)
    "#{namespace}-pagination-contents-#{page_number}"
  end

  def with_manual_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page)
      end)
    end
  end

  def with_automatic_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, paginate_on_scroll: true, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page, activate_when_observed: true)
      end)
    end
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_tag(day_timeline, &)
    turbo_frame_tag day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day_timeline.day), data: { timeline_target: "frame" }, role: "presentation", refresh: :morph, &
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day)
    "day-timeline-pagination-contents-#{day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")}"
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_link(day_timeline, filter)
    if day_timeline.next_day
      link_to t("helpers_ui.pagination.load_more"), events_days_path(day: day_timeline.next_day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), **filter.as_params),
        class: "day-timeline-pagination-link", data: { frame: day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day_timeline.next_day), pagination_target: "paginationLink" }
    end
  end

  private
    def pagination_list(name, tag_element: :div, paginate_on_scroll: false, **properties, &block)
      classes = properties.delete(:class)
      properties[:id] ||= "#{name}-pagination-list"
      tag.public_send tag_element,
        class: token_list(name, "display-contents", classes),
        data: { controller: "pagination", pagination_paginate_on_intersection_value: paginate_on_scroll },
        **properties,
        &block
    end

    def default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed)
      t("helpers_ui.pagination.load_more")
    end
end
EOF

**Internationalization Milestone Achieved!**

Wow, check this out! Zero failures in the 39 helper tests! And get this, the English baseline is perfect across all 41 screens and emails - **ZERO DIFFERENCES**! Plus, RuboCop is giving us a clean bill of health – **ZERO OFFENSES**!

Okay, time to dive into the next phase: internationalizing those six mailers and their templates. I need to meticulously review every single one: from `AccountMailer#cancellation` and its templates, to `UserMailer#email_change_confirmation` in `app/mailers/` and the associated views in both `app/views/mailers/` and `app/views/user_mailer/`. That's a lot of files!

I'm thinking about the details already. For `Notification::BundleMailer`, I need to pay extra attention to `notification.html.erb` and `notification.text.erb`. Remember that time formatting? Yeah, using `I18n.l(@bundle.starts_at, format: :bundle_since)` yields `"Notifications since 9am on Wednesday, March 5"` in English and `"3月5日(水) 午前9時以降の通知"` in Japanese, which is fantastic! And I'll need to remember to update how we handle the pluralization of notifications using `t("mailers.bundle.new_notifications_count", count: @notifications.count)`. I'll want to ensure that it behaves correctly for all locales.

And let's not forget that clever use of `<%= "-" * board.name.length %>` for that text separator in `notification.text.erb`. It's robust and handles any string!

So, the plan: create the `config/locales/{en,ja}/mailers.yml` files, update all 6 mailers and all 15 templates, and then run those tests – `bin/rails test test/mailers`, followed by `VERIFY_BASELINE=1 bin/rails test /tmp/capture_english_baseline.rb`, and finally, a good dose of `bin/rubocop`. steps.message: Let's create `config/locales/{en,ja}/views_layouts_auth_public.yml`, update all layouts, auth, join_codes, public, active_storage, and pwa templates, and verify our exact English baseline!
steps.reasoning_content:
**Internationalization Deep Dive: Phase 1 Complete (Almost!)**

Okay, here's the game plan: the mailer tests are all green, and the English baseline snapshots are pristine - no diffs! A clean slate, excellent!

Now, it's time to tackle the big internationalization push. I'm going to take a very focused, iterative approach to ensure absolute accuracy. My strategy is to break this down into four distinct, manageable sub-steps for the views, layouts, Turbo Streams, and the PWA manifest. After *each* sub-step, I'll immediately verify the English baseline using `VERIFY_BASELINE=1 bin/rails test /tmp/capture_english_baseline.rb`. The goal? To catch any subtle drifts in the English strings *immediately* and fix them. No surprises later.

Here's the sub-step breakdown:

*   **Sub-step 2E-1:** Layouts, Sessions, Signups, Join Codes, Public Views, ActiveStorage, PWA (using the `views_layouts_auth_public.yml` locale file).
*   **Sub-step 2E-2:** Account, Boards, Entropy (using `views_account_boards.yml`).
*   **Sub-step 2E-3:** Cards, Reactions (using `views_cards_reactions.yml`).
*   **Sub-step 2E-4:** Bar, Events, Filters, Searches, Tags, My, Notifications, Users, Webhooks (using `views_events_filters_my_users_webhooks.yml`).

Once all four sub-steps are done, I'm going to run a full audit across the entire codebase using an automated AST/HTML/ERB script. This script will scour every file in `app/views/`, `app/helpers/`, `app/controllers/`, `app/models/`, `app/mailers/`, `app/javascript/`, and `lib/` to flag *any* hardcoded English strings or attributes like `placeholder`, `title`, `alt`, `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `for-screen-reader`, `data-turbo-confirm`, `data-bridge-title`, `data-combobox-*`, `data-multi-selection-combobox-*`, or even the `@page_title` variable. This audit is crucial to ensure *complete* internationalization. No room for slippage.

Right now, I'm going to kick off **Sub-step 2E-1**. I've identified the files that need attention:

*   `app/views/layouts/_lightbox.html.erb`
*   `app/views/layouts/application.html.erb` (specifically the "Skip to main content" link)
*   `app/views/layouts/public.html.erb` ("Skip to main content" again)
*   `app/views/layouts/shared/_colophon.html.erb`
*   `app/views/layouts/shared/_welcome_letter.html.erb`
*   `app/views/active_storage/blobs/_blob.html.erb` ("Download #{blob.filename}", "Download")
*   `app/views/active_storage/blobs/web/_representation.html.erb` ("unknown" file extension)
*   `app/views/events/event/attachments/_attachment.html.erb` ("unknown" file extension)
*   `app/views/pwa/manifest.json.erb`
*   All files in `sessions/`, `signups/`, `join_codes/`, and `public/boards/`

My next immediate action is to write the `config/locales/{en,ja}/views_layouts_auth_public.yml` locale files, update the corresponding templates in `app/views/`, and then run the baseline verification test. This is the first, but essential, step in ensuring everything is translated correctly, from the application layout down to the blobs that are downloaded. I am eager to get started with this.

steps.message: Let's run Audit 1 (static ERB/Ruby scan for any leftover hardcoded English text or attributes) and Audit 3 (full `:en` vs `:ja` key parity & interpolation variable check).
steps.reasoning_content:
**Internationalization Triumph and Rigorous Audits**

Okay, wow! Just... *wow*. I can't believe it! All 332 view files, the 30 helpers, the 6 mailers, the 15 mailer templates, those 17 controllers, the models, and every single JavaScript file are fully internationalized. And the golden baseline test, that beast across 41 screens and emails? *Zero* differences. It's a huge win, but we're not done yet. We've come too far to slack! We have to make sure we've caught every edge case.

First up, is **Audit 1**: We're hitting the static code with a string scanner. It's time to comb through those ERB, HTML, and Ruby files in `app/views/`, `app/helpers/`, `app/controllers/`, and `app/mailers/`, stripping out all the code blocks and meticulously examining any literal English text or attributes like `placeholder=`, `title=`, `alt=`, and more. We need to catch everything, from a stray string in an `aria-label` to that sneaky bit of text within a `turbo_confirm:`.

The second audit, **Audit 2**, is where we make sure we render everything with `?locale=ja` or `identity.locale = "ja"`. I want to test *everything* rendered live in Japanese with Nokogiri. Every screen, every email (both HTML and text!). We have to consider every single route from `config/routes.rb`!! We're going to use Nokogiri to parse the rendered HTML and pull out *every* visible text node and attribute. This includes `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `placeholder`, `title`, `alt`, and other form attributes. We'll mark any English words, except for fixture data like names or common hotkeys.

Finally, we'll dive into **Audit 3**: a translation key parity and interpolation audit between `:en` and `:ja`. We want to make sure the translations are all accounted for and that all the interpolations are working correctly between these locales.

Okay, let's get those first and third audits running right now! It's showtime.

arguments.command:
bin/rails runner '
# Audit 3: Key parity and interpolation parity between :en and :ja
I18n.backend.eager_load!
translations = I18n.backend.send(:translations)

def flatten_hash(h, prefix = "")
  h.each_with_object({}) do |(k, v), out|
    key = prefix.empty? ? k.to_s : "#{prefix}.#{k}"
    if v.is_a?(Hash)
      out.merge!(flatten_hash(v, key))
    else
      out[key] = v
    end
  end
end

# Compare all custom namespaces we defined
custom_files_en = Dir["config/locales/en/*.yml", "config/locales/en.yml"].each_with_object({}) do |f, acc|
  acc.merge!(flatten_hash(YAML.load_file(f)["en"] || {}))
end
custom_files_ja = Dir["config/locales/ja/*.yml", "config/locales/ja.yml"].each_with_object({}) do |f, acc|
  acc.merge!(flatten_hash(YAML.load_file(f)["ja"] || {}))
end

missing_in_ja = custom_files_en.keys - custom_files_ja.keys
puts "Missing in JA: #{missing_in_ja.inspect}"

interp_mismatches = []
custom_files_en.each do |k, en_val|
  ja_val = custom_files_ja[k]
  next unless en_val.is_a?(String) && ja_val.is_a?(String)
  en_vars = en_val.scan(/%\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten.sort.uniq
  ja_vars = ja_val.scan(/%\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten.sort.uniq
  # Pluralization "one:" in English often omits %{count}, which is fine
  en_vars -= ["count"] if k.end_with?(".one")
  ja_vars -= ["count"] if k.end_with?(".one")
  if en_vars != ja_vars
    interp_mismatches << [k, en_vars, ja_vars]
  end
end
puts "Interpolation mismatches: #{interp_mismatches.inspect}"
' && ruby -e '
# Audit 1: Static scan of all ERB views for leftover English outside ERB tags or inside attributes
Dir.glob("app/views/**/*.{erb,jbuilder}").sort.each do |file|
  next if file == "app/views/prompts/commands/index.html.erb" || file == "app/views/prompts/commands/_command.html.erb"
  raw = File.read(file)
  # Check hardcoded attributes in ERB calls
  raw.lines.each_with_index do |line, idx|
    next if line =~ /^\s*<%#/
    if line =~ /(@page_title\s*=\s*"|placeholder:\s*"|turbo_confirm:\s*"|bridge_title:\s*"|aria:\s*\{\s*label:\s*"|title:\s*"[A-Za-z]|alt:\s*"[A-Za-z])/
      puts "ATTR #{file}:#{idx+1}: #{line.strip}"
    end
  end
  next unless file.end_with?(".html.erb", ".text.erb", ".turbo_stream.erb")
  stripped = raw
    .gsub(/<%#.*?%>/m, "")
    .gsub(/<style\b.*?<\/style>/m, "")
    .gsub(/<script\b.*?<\/script>/m, "")
    .gsub(/<svg\b.*?<\/svg>/m, "")
    .gsub(/<%=?.*?%>/m, " ")
    .gsub(/<[^>]+>/m, " ")
    .gsub(/&(nbsp|middot|larr|rarr|amp|gt|lt);/, " ")
  words = stripped.scan(/[A-Za-z]{2,}/) - %w[Fizzy Basecamp HEY RE DEV HMAC SHA256]
  unless words.empty?
    puts "TEXT #{file}: #{words.inspect}"
  end
end
'

steps.reasoning_content:
**Initial Assessment: Deep Dive into Japanese Localization**

Okay, *whoa*. Just look at this static scan output! The initial checks for missing translations and interpolation mismatches are coming up clean, but that doesn't mean everything's perfect. Diving into the `app/views/` directory across those 385 files, the `ATTR` matches are alarmingly sparse – only `placeholder` attributes with those specific placeholder values. Nothing else! No untranslated `placeholder`, `title`, `alt`, `aria-label`, `turbo-confirm`, `bridge_title`, or even the `@page_title` that I was expecting. And the `TEXT` matches were hilariously limited, just grabbing those HTML tags with the `keydown.esc->dialog#close` data-action attribute – that regex needs serious tweaking!

So, to *really* understand the scope of this, I need to go beyond the naive static analysis. Time to run **Audit 2**. I'm going to render every single screen and email, setting the locale to Japanese (`?locale=ja` or `identity.locale = "ja"`). Then, parse *every single rendered document* using Nokogiri. Crucially, I'll inspect *every* text node and every single readable attribute – `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `placeholder`, `title`, `alt`, the `value` on submit buttons (which often holds the button text),  `data-turbo-confirm`, `data-bridge-title`, the `data-combobox` attributes, the `data-boards-form-self-removal-prompt-message-value`, and `data-validation-message`, and `data-touch-placeholder-placeholder-value`. This will give me a comprehensive picture of what's *actually* localized and what's missed. Time to get this audit underway.

Next, we address unsupported locales:

Third, the default English:

Fourth, we'll make sure we translate our static error pages.

Finally, we hit the big one: comprehensive Japanese translation!

*   We'll audit the DOM and attributes across all screens and emails to ensure Japanese text, dates, screen-reader announcements, and all relevant attributes (`aria-label`, `.for-screen-reader`, `alt`, `title`, `placeholder`) are fully translated. We'll verify correct fragment caching isolation. We will also address Turbo broadcast/push notifications, too.
*   We'll use a translation key parity test to make sure our English and Japanese keys match up perfectly and correctly interpolate.
*   And finally, we'll build a headless Chrome system test to verify client-side JavaScript, especially the `local_time_controller.js`, and its date and relative time formatting, confirming the use of Japanese format when `?locale=ja` is activated, and returning to English when nothing was selected. We will also be sure to test `bubble_controller.js`, `multi_selection_combobox_controller.js`, and `turbo_navigation_controller.js` and clean browser sign-in!

require "test_helper"

class I18nCompletenessTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "all custom English translation keys exist in Japanese with matching interpolations" do
    en_keys = load_locale_files("en")
    ja_keys = load_locale_files("ja")

    missing_in_ja = en_keys.keys - ja_keys.keys
    assert_empty missing_in_ja, "Keys missing in Japanese locale: #{missing_in_ja.join(', ')}"

    mismatches = []
    en_keys.each do |key, en_val|
      ja_val = ja_keys[key]
      next unless en_val.is_a?(String) && ja_val.is_a?(String)

      en_vars = en_val.scan(/%\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten.sort.uniq
      ja_vars = ja_val.scan(/%\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten.sort.uniq
      if key.end_with?(".one")
        en_vars -= [ "count" ]
        ja_vars -= [ "count" ]
      end

      mismatches << "#{key}: en=#{en_vars.inspect} ja=#{ja_vars.inspect}" if en_vars != ja_vars
    end

    assert_empty mismatches, "Interpolation variable mismatches:\n#{mismatches.join("\n")}"
  end

  test "static error pages render in both English and Japanese" do
    %w[ 400.html 404.html 406-unsupported-browser.html 422.html 500.html ].each do |filename|
      doc = Nokogiri::HTML5(File.read(Rails.root.join("public", filename)))
      en_text = doc.css("[lang='en']").map(&:text).join(" ")
      ja_text = doc.css("[lang='ja']").map(&:text).join(" ")

      assert_match(/[A-Za-z]{3,}/, en_text, "Expected English text in public/#{filename}")
      assert_match(/[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Han}]/, ja_text, "Expected Japanese text in public/#{filename}")
    end
  end

  test "push notification payload and live broadcast use recipient locale" do
    identities(:kevin).update_locale("ja")

    # Triggered while current locale is English (e.g. David in English)
    I18n.with_locale(:en) do
      notification = Notification.create!(
        user: users(:kevin),
        creator: users(:david),
        source: events(:logo_published),
        account: accounts("37s")
      )

      payload = nil
      users(:kevin).in_locale { payload = notification.payload.to_h }
      assert_includes payload[:body], "Davidが追加しました"
    end
  end

  private
    def load_locale_files(locale)
      files = Dir[Rails.root.join("config/locales/#{locale}.yml"), Rails.root.join("config/locales/#{locale}/*.yml")]
      files.each_with_object({}) do |file, acc|
        data = YAML.load_file(file)[locale] || {}
        acc.merge!(flatten_keys(data))
      end
    end

    def flatten_keys(hash, prefix = "")
      hash.each_with_object({}) do |(key, value), result|
        full_key = prefix.empty? ? key.to_s : "#{prefix}.#{key}"
        if value.is_a?(Hash)
          result.merge!(flatten_keys(value, full_key))
        else
          result[full_key] = value
        end
      end
    end
end
EOF

        ActionText::RichText.all.map { |rt| rt.to_plain_text.strip }
      ).compact.reject(&:empty?).uniq.sort_by { |w| -w.length }
    end

    def audit_japanese_html(screen, html_str, fixture_strings, findings)
      doc = Nokogiri::HTML5(html_str)
      doc.css("script, style").remove
      doc.xpath("//text()").each do |node|
        check_japanese_text(screen, "<#{node.parent.name}>", node.text, fixture_strings, findings)
      end
      doc.css("*").each do |el|
        READABLE_ATTRS.each do |attr|
          check_japanese_text(screen, "#{el.name}[#{attr}]", el[attr], fixture_strings, findings) if el[attr]
        end
        if el.name == "input" && %w[ submit button ].include?(el["type"]) && el["value"]
          check_japanese_text(screen, "input[value]", el["value"], fixture_strings, findings)
        end
      end
    end

    def check_japanese_text(screen, context, text, fixture_strings, findings)
      cleaned = text.to_s.strip
      return if cleaned.empty?

      cleaned = cleaned.gsub(/https?:\/\/\S+/, "")
      fixture_strings.each { |w| cleaned.gsub!(/#{Regexp.escape(w)}/i, "") }
      ALLOWED_ENGLISH.sort_by { |w| -w.length }.each { |w| cleaned.gsub!(/#{Regexp.escape(w)}/i, "") }
      cleaned.gsub!(/#\d+/, "")
      return if cleaned.strip =~ /\A[A-Za-z0-9\W]\z/

      english_runs = cleaned.scan(/[A-Za-z]{2,}(?:\s+[A-Za-z]{2,})*/)
      unless english_runs.empty?
        findings << "[#{screen}] #{context}: #{text.to_s.strip.inspect} -> #{english_runs.inspect}"
      end
    end
end
